fix_commit_message:
Bug 1941876 - Fix handling of dynamic elements when swapping objects r=jandem

There are two problems here. Firstly, swapping a nursery and a tenured object
can leave dynamic element buffers with the wrong ownership kind. For example
we could have a tenured object with a nursery-owned buffer. This could cause
UAF if the buffer we collected in the next nursery collection.

Secondly, the code to copy dynamic elements doesn't account for shifted
elements.

I added the testcase but also updated the testObjectSwap JSAPI test to catch
this problem. The change to BufferAllocator::checkChunkGCStateNotInUse is to
speed up this test.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D234513
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix f2c46512ec48 on top of intro c002e9bc863c via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UseAfterFree): The prepareForSwap function only copies dynamic element buffers when the buffer is inside the nursery (ChunkPtrIsInsideNursery), but fails to consider the case where a tenured object with a buffer marked as nursery-owned is swapped with a nursery object. When swapping a nursery object with a tenured object, the tenured object can end up with a pointer to a buffer that is marked as nursery-owned. During the next nursery collection, this buffer will be freed because the GC believes it belongs to the nursery, causing a use-after-free when the tenured object later accesses the freed buffer. Root cause: The introduction of the buffer allocator for JSObject elements changed how dynamic element buffers are managed during object swaps. The new code only copies buffers when they are physically inside the nursery memory region, but fails to consider cases where a buffer is allocated via AllocBuffer with nursery ownership semantics. When swapping objects between nursery and tenured heaps, the buffer ownership metadata can become inconsistent with the object's heap location, causing the GC to incorrectly free the buffer. The secondary issue is that shifted elements (array elements that have been logically removed from the front) are not accounted for when copying the buffer.
